DEFECT (must-fix, non-blocking): the ~46% structural-fraction figure is NOT reproducible under any single consistent counting convention. Doc writes eponymy(55)+boundary(26)=~46% of errors. 55 = TYPE_MISMATCH both-sides (FN24+FP31); 26 = BOUNDARY ONE side only (table shows FN26|FP26=52). Denominator 175 = FN87+FP88 = both-sides. Mixing both-sides eponymy(55) with one-side boundary(26) gives 81/175=0.463; the consistent both-sides figure is (55+52)/175=0.611=~61%. The 46% is an inconsistent-convention artifact.

DEFECT IMPACT IS CONSERVATIVE (why non-blocking): the true both-sides structural mass (~61%) is LARGER than the doc claim (~46%). The deliverable conclusion is structural-ceiling / data-cannot-fix / external-data-needed. A larger structural share strengthens that conclusion, so the arithmetic slip understates rather than inflates the case. It does not flip the verdict on the gate (A) ceiling 0.724 nor (C) integrity. Recommend correcting the line to read both-sides ~61% (or relabel as one-side count consistently) before final commit.
